items.title: Hal Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: I heard Elvis Presley, I remember Bill Haley and the Comets and all that, it just never did anything for me.

ctx.x: So it was just kind of a happy music, and it wasn’t a protest music like rock & roll. I heard Elvis Presley, I remember Bill Haley and the Comets and all that, it just never did anything for me. And I like ragtime and the banjo music and all that kind of thing, and that’s what led me into an appreciation of Dixieland, when I finally, I heard the Firehouse Five at Disneyland, when we moved to California when I was eight. I was taken to Disneyland for my birthday, the first live jazz band I ever heard, that’s it.…
And you were playing at that time, which instrument were you playing?
